binding_note: r1 (message_reactions) binds the reacting user (r0) to r2, the OOM message; r2.channel_id ties to r3 (#engineering); r3.team_id ties to r4 (the workspace); r5 (user_teams) is a separate membership row tied to r4 only through team_id, identifying the workspace as the one where Robert Walsh holds an admin membership, without requiring r5's user to equal r0. Two workspace members share the first name Morgan and both satisfy reactor+message+channel+workspace conditions, leaving r0 unresolved between them.

obligations.name: identify_reacting_morgan
obligations.description: Select the workspace member named Morgan who left an 'eyes' reaction on Lukas's circuit-tracer OOM message, in the #engineering channel of the workspace where Robert Walsh holds an admin membership; two same-named candidates leave the selection unresolved.

task_spec.text: Identify which Morgan left the eyes reaction on Lukas's circuit-tracer OOM message in #engineering, in the workspace where Robert Walsh is an admin.

access_plan: Use conversations.history on #engineering (C03IJKL9012) to locate Lukas's circuit-tracer OOM message, then reactions.get on that message's timestamp/channel to list reactors and their emoji names. Cross-reference reactor IDs against users.list (or users.info) filtered by display/real name 'Morgan' to find the matching candidate(s). Confirm the workspace via channels.list/conversations.info (channel's team_id) and confirm Robert Walsh's admin membership via users.info's workspace association, establishing the workspace scope independently of the reacting user's own membership.
